patch.value: Pilot Fleet CI v2 quick PR and exhaustive local tiers

Companion: pm-cli-website-dyhg. Preserve exhaustive default and release validation while reducing PR duplication; measure quick/full coverage and required check latency. Isolated from release caller migration PR #257.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Inspection: #254 both Node jobs failed solely because the 500-case column-ownership corpus exceeded a 2400000ms test timeout. gh --log-failed returned empty; individual jobs API logs confirmed it. Replacing seeded corpus timeouts with explicit seed and transition budgets; no product latency contract is weakened, so no time-scale env is needed. Quick mode uses seeds 1..50 versus 1..500 across seven property loops. accept:packed already proves Bun project/global installs and bunx ephemeral CLI plus tarball extension installs with CSV IO. No standalone markdown/docs checker exists. Release migration PR #257 files remain untouched.

# Fleet CI v2 pilot

The two required checks remain `test (22)` and `test (26)` on GitHub-hosted
runners. Only PRs and manual dispatch start this tier. Superseded PR runs cancel.
Docs/tracker-only PRs keep both checks green by running their applicable gates.
There is no standalone markdown checker in this package.

| Check | Code PR Node 22 | Code PR Node 26 | Docs/tracker-only PR (both) | Deep Node 22 + 26 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm ci / prepare merge drivers | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Strict tracker health / merge drivers | — | yes | yes | yes |
| Release workflow verification | — | yes | — | npm + Bun gates |
| Build + test suite | quick | quick via coverage | — | full, npm + Bun |
| Typecheck, lint, duplicates, docstrings | — | yes | — | npm + Bun gates |
| Coverage, unchanged 100% lines/branches/functions | — | quick | — | full, npm + Bun |
| Production audit, pack dry-run | — | yes | — | npm + Bun gates |
| Packed consumer acceptance | via tests | via tests + gate | — | npm + Bun gates |
| Changelog consistency | — | yes | yes | npm + Bun gates |
| Publish attestation / changelog date verification | — | yes | — | npm + Bun gates |
| Bun package-graph install | — | yes | — | yes |
| CodeQL | changed source paths | changed source paths | skipped | separate weekly scan |

Deep runs on main pushes, daily at 02:47 UTC, and manual dispatch. It never
blocks PRs. Local jobs queue even when local slots are busy; the fleet controller
sets `PM_LOCAL_DEEP=off` only after no local host has been reachable for ten
minutes. The fallback is GitHub-hosted. Deep concurrency cancels older runs of
the same ref and the job timeout is 120 minutes. Release remains at 03:23 UTC;
weekly CodeQL remains at 03:17 UTC on Monday, including lockfile-only changes.

`PM_TEST_DEPTH=quick` selects the first 50 of each existing 500-case deterministic
sequence. `full`, an unset variable, and any unrecognized value keep full depth.
The helper uses one tenth (rounded up), with a floor of 25 capped by the original
count. Batch sizes and seed generation stay unchanged; the last batch can be
partial. All per-case assertions remain. Plain `npm test`, `prepublishOnly` and
the release gate remain exhaustive unless their caller explicitly opts in.

The local-runner pilot (#254, run 43623045892) failed on both Node versions
because column ownership exceeded its fixed 2,400,000 ms test timeout. Individual
job logs confirmed this as the only failing test; `gh --log-failed` returned no
content. Seeded corpus tests now terminate by seed and transition counts, with
the workflow guarding total job time. Those tests do not prove a latency SLA.
No product time contract needed scaling, so no `PM_TEST_TIME_SCALE` was added.

`accept:packed` already installs the tarball using Bun project and global
installs and the bunx ephemeral host CLI, then exercises CSV operations. It also
covers npm/npx and minimum/development host versions. The PR gate therefore needs
only `bun install --no-save` afterwards, not another Bun release gate. The packed
acceptance test and standalone gate are both retained as requested; these are a
remaining source of duplication within the existing gate.

## Applying this to another package

1. Create a package-owned Task tagged `ci,performance`, link the companion item,
   and work in a fresh branch/worktree. Inspect open work and reserve files owned
   by other changes before editing.
2. Read `package.json` scripts, coverage source scope/thresholds, engine floor,
   test runner, packed acceptance, and workflow contract tests. Inventory every
   check in the current release gate; use the table above as a checklist, not an
   assumption about the sibling's scripts.
3. Search tests with `rg -n 'seed|random|for .*<[=]?|length:|timeout|Date.now|performance.now' test`.
   Read CI job timing/logs and test durations to rank expensive suites. Separate
   fixed memory/row-boundary fixtures from repetitive property corpora: do not
   shrink a million-row memory-contract test merely because its count is large.
4. Copy the tiny depth helper. Replace every large property-loop count, keeping
   seed expressions and batch sizes identical. Update expected counts and
   diagnostics. Support a partial final batch and retain all assertions. Default
   depth must be full. Remove machine-speed deadlines from finite corpora; use
   operation budgets. Scale only real product time contracts with a documented
   env factor when necessary.
5. Run quick coverage at the original thresholds. Turn late-seed-only branches
   into small explicit deterministic regression cases; never weaken thresholds
   or add exclusions. Run full coverage separately on the same host and record
   both complete command wall times and host contention caveats.
6. Copy the PR workflow's concurrency, hosted routing, Node 22/26 required job
   names, full checkout and NUL-safe base...head change detection as fixed
   template. Adapt the docs allowlist/check commands, Node floor, release gate
   and Bun smoke to the package. Inspect packed acceptance before omitting an
   extra bunx smoke. Even the engines-floor tests may require Bun setup when
   the suite runs packed acceptance internally.
7. Copy the deep workflow triggers, controller-owned runner expression,
   per-ref cancellation, 120-minute timeout, explicit full depth, and npm/Bun
   matrix gates. Pick a per-repository off-peak cron minute distinct from its
   release and CodeQL schedules. Never add a PR trigger or required deep check.
8. Copy CodeQL tracker/docs/lockfile path exclusions on push and PR, retain its
   weekly schedule and pinned actions, and use PR cancellation. Adapt lockfile
   names if the sibling has additional lockfiles.
9. Run typecheck, lint, touched tests, quick/full coverage, changelog check and
   the quick release gate. Run actionlint if installed, otherwise parse YAML and
   record that narrower validation. Link and execute tests through pm as well.
10. Wait for the shared dispatch hold, verify commit identity/privacy, push and
    open the PR. Measure jobs API `created_at` to `completed_at` for both required
    checks, including queueing; investigate and fix any result above 15 minutes.
    Record execution-only time separately if useful. Attempt branch dispatch of
    the deep workflow once; a new workflow absent on main may refuse dispatch.
    Report that refusal without a workaround. Release the tracker claim; leave
    the item open and let the orchestrator handle reviews and merge.

value.text: Typecheck and lint passed. All three edited workflows parsed with the installed yaml parser (actionlint unavailable). Strict health on this development checkout reports an ignored installed pm-github extension/host version skew; this is existing local extension state, not tracked CI state. Will verify health with isolated global configuration. Quick coverage is running; full coverage will follow sequentially to avoid self-contention.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Strict health passes with isolated global configuration; the normal developer-global configuration has an unrelated installed extension version skew already tracked by pm-csv-sdyz. Changelog consistency passes. Initial quick coverage found a sampled-roundtrip aggregate expecting too many events for 50 seeds; its required minimum now scales linearly (full still at least 20, quick at least 2), retaining all per-case comparisons. Million-row memory contract remains unchanged and passes. Initial failed-pass timings will not be used as successful benchmarks.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Deep job id is deliberately deep, producing deep (22) and deep (26). This keeps a manual branch dispatch from emitting the required test (22)/test (26) contexts and accidentally blocking a PR. Existing CodeQL per-ref PR cancellation was already correct and is retained. Change detection necessarily follows checkout and is the first decision before tool setup/install.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The seventh change-detection scenario found and fixed a source-to-docs rename bypass: git name-only with default rename folding emitted only the new docs pathname. Adding --no-renames preserves the deleted source path and correctly selects code=true. The regression fixture demonstrates false before, true after. This is necessary to uphold docs-only gating rather than a design deviation.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Slow-hardware hardening also removes the packed-acceptance wrapper test/process deadlines (600/590 seconds). Its fixed host/scenario loops and exact receipt assertions define the work, not elapsed time; the workflow job remains bounded at 120 minutes. #254 passed that test at 471.71 seconds, already close to the old cap. This is preventative removal of the same machine-speed failure class, not an additional failure claimed from #254. The edit precedes this coverage run loading that test file.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Timing correction to the preceding comment: process inspection shows packed acceptance launched at nearly the same moment as the wrapper edit, so this quick pass may have loaded the old stricter cap. Both following full coverage and quick release gates will load the updated wrapper, and the touched packed test will also be run explicitly. Assertions and scenario counts are identical in either wrapper; no further runtime-source edits during the measurements.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Observed local failure confirms the packed-wrapper deadline problem: the in-flight quick pass loaded the old wrapper and its subprocess was killed at 590.159 seconds. The guard removal had landed after that test process parsed its source. This failed run is excluded from successful timing evidence; rerun quick coverage on frozen final test sources before full coverage and the quick release gate. No source thresholds or assertion scopes changed.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Cheap-path audit found existing documentation checks embedded in test/packaging.test.ts and test/shipped-changelog.test.ts, rather than a standalone markdown script. The docs path now runs those plus test/identity-audit.test.ts, preserving public commit/privacy checks for tracker-only PRs. Written design exception: .agents/pm/verify-release-yaml.mjs must select the code path because it is executable release-verification code inside the tracker root; treating it as tracker data would skip the check it can break. The verifier and PR #257 files themselves remain untouched.
